title: Second appeal to the Board of Revenue, Ajmer — dismissal four months ago, receipt in the file

input.text: Sir, previous advocate ne Collector ke saamne appeal haar di, order aaya lagbhag chaar mahine pehle. Client Bhilwara se hai, zameen agricultural, jamabandi dispute. Ab Board of Revenue, Ajmer ke paas second appeal karna hai. File mein ek receipt hai 'appeal fee paid' jiski date pehle order se pehle ki hai — previous advocate bola yehi proof hai ki appeal time par thi. Certified copy Collector order ki hai, but limitation period client ko nahi pata. Vakalatnama purana hai. Client kahta hai 'Board mein jeet jayenge, civil court mat jaana'. Kya second appeal maintainable hai, kitne din bache, aur receipt se kya hota hai?
attachments: Fee receipt (date earlier than the Collector order)

triage.oneLineRead: A possible Board of Revenue second appeal is already late on its face; a receipt that predates the impugned order cannot prove timely filing, and the appeal chapter of the Land Revenue Act is still PENDING in this fixture.

issueMap.issue: Whether a second appeal lies to the Board of Revenue from this Collector order
issueMap.note: Depends on the exact provision under which the Collector sat. Do not assume every Collector order is second-appealable.
The Act's appeal chapter numbers are PENDING. Four months is a red flag, not a computed period.

issueMap.issue: Whether the fee receipt saves limitation
issueMap.note: A receipt dated before the Collector order cannot be the filing of an appeal against that order.

issueMap.issue: Whether condonation under Limitation Act s. 5 is available
issueMap.note: s. 29(2) interaction with special revenue limitation is PENDING. Do not invent the answer.

verification.proposition: Appeals and second appeals in revenue matters lie as provided in the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act
verification.provision: Rajasthan Land Revenue Act 1956, appeal chapter (section numbers PENDING)
verification.sourceUrlNote: Read the current bare Act. Do not copy a remembered section number into a memo of appeal.

verification.provision: Limitation Act 1963, s. 5 read with s. 29(2)
verification.sourceUrlNote: Whether s. 5 is excluded by the Land Revenue Act is the whole question; it is not settled in this fixture.

checklist: Bare Act of Rajasthan Land Revenue Act 1956 (current reprint) — appeal / second-appeal chapter
Exact provision under which the Collector sat
Certified copy endorsement date vs order date vs four-month oral estimate
Whether any first-appeal memo and diary number exist
Fresh vakalatnama for Board of Revenue
Whether a civil suit is already pending on the same jamabandi

terminalOutcome.label: Hold the second appeal until the Act is read and the receipt is explained
terminalOutcome.rationale: Four months plus a receipt that predates the order is a limitation trap. Filing today with a guessed section number would be the previous advocate's error, repeated.
terminalOutcome.nextAction: Read the appeal chapter, compute limitation from the certified-copy dates (not from memory), and only then decide condonation vs. a different forum.

teachingNotes: Revenue second appeals die of the wrong ladder more often than of the wrong ground.
A fee receipt is not a filing. If it is dated before the order, it is evidence of a different payment.
Section numbers left PENDING are the lesson. Inventing them is how a Board of Revenue memo gets returned.
commonMistakes: Citing a remembered section from an old commentary.
Treating the receipt as proof of limitation.
Filing in civil court because 'Board will take time'.
Using the old vakalatnama without a Board-specific appointment.
seniorVariants: Tabulate order date, certified-copy date, and statutory period in one line before any ground of appeal.
If s. 5 is unavailable, say so and stop — do not dress a dead appeal as a writ without a supervising revenue lawyer.
Ask whether the Collector order is appealable at all; some orders are revisable, not appealable.

accuracy.adverseFact: The only dated paper that looks like 'we filed in time' is a receipt from before the Collector order. If that is the previous advocate's limitation story, it collapses on inspection.
